about.title: Lakewood Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Grief does not follow a schedule, but California's legal system does. That tension is why so many Lakewood families reach out to us. A wrongful death claim is a civil action brought by a spouse, domestic partner, children, or certain dependents after a preventable loss, and it moves forward whether or not prosecutors ever file criminal charges. Public records show Lakewood logged 308 injury collisions and 441 injured people in 2025, along with one traffic death, with Del Amo Boulevard, South Street, Woodruff Avenue, and Carson Street carrying the largest share of reported crashes. Yet fatal negligence is not limited to roadways; it also reaches workplaces, care facilities, and hospitals across Los Angeles County. Through a claim, surviving family members may seek funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the deceased would have provided, and compensation for lost love, companionship, and guidance. We work on contingency, so no fee is owed unless your family obtains a recovery.

items.title: Clarity on who may file
items.desc: California limits standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. We can explain where your family fits before any step is taken.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is far shorter when a government entity is involved. We move quickly to protect your options.

items.title: Losses that are fully accounted for
items.desc: Recoverable damages go beyond funeral and burial costs to include lost financial support and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. We document each of these carefully.

items.question: My loved one died in a crash on Del Amo Boulevard. Does the city's involvement change the deadline?
items.answer: It might. If a public agency such as the City of Lakewood, Los Angeles County, or Caltrans could share responsibility for a roadway condition, a formal claim must be presented to that agency on a much shorter timeline than the standard two years. We can review the collision report and determine quickly whether a government claim applies.

items.question: The driver is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to end?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action with its own deadline, and it does not depend on a conviction. Many families pursue both paths at the same time, and evidence gathered in one can sometimes support the other.

items.question: What does it cost to contact you?
items.answer: Nothing. Our initial consultation is free, and we work on contingency, meaning we are paid only if your family obtains a recovery. You can discuss fee terms directly during your first conversation.
